steps.title: Welcome
steps.body: A short setup to get this app ready. Nothing here is required; you can close it and come back later.

steps.title: Load example data?
steps.body: Example data fills the lists, detail pages and dashboards so you can see the app working straight away. Each card has its own Load button. Pick "None" on a production install.

store._note: Configuration exchange, not rows. A configuration set carries the registers, schemas, objects, views, flows, sources and mappings that make one way of working hold together. There is deliberately NO `installable` allowlist: a set exists to introduce schemas the instance does not have YET, so listing schemas this app already owns would refuse exactly the sets worth installing. The trust boundary for a bundle is its publisher, enforced by the engine's source allowlist and trusted-key check. ⚠️ An EMPTY `installable` means install NOTHING, not install anything — omitting the key and declaring an empty list are different things.

pages.title: Marketplace

config.title: Marketplace
config.description: Install document configurations that other organisations have published: a template set, an anonymisation policy, or the flows behind a signature.

pages._note: ADR-114 Decision 4 / ADR-080. Declarative: openregister hosts the store plane, so this app writes NO store controller. With no registry configured the page renders the app's built-in items and makes NO network call.

pages.title: Dashboard
pages._note: DashboardIndex is a self-contained view that renders a single CnDashboardPage (KPI cards + recent-activity list + quick-anonymization panel). It is mounted via type:"custom" so only one CnDashboardPage renders — wrapping it as a body widget of a type:"dashboard" page nested CnDashboardPage-in-CnDashboardPage (hydra dashboard-antipattern).

pages.title: Document comparison
pages._note: Side-by-side document comparison (original vs anonymised output). Standalone page; no nav item; deep-linked with ?left=&right= file-id query params.

pages.title: Versions
pages._note: Document versions (Versies) — thin consumer of Nextcloud files_versions. Part of the ADR-001 document-detail family; standalone deep-linked page (?fileId=) like Comparison, no nav item. Lists/opens/downloads/restores/compares a document's file versions.

pages.title: Component gallery
pages._note: Living design-system reference for the reusable Dd* components (each shown with its variants/states). Self-contained view; standalone deep-linked page (/gallery), no nav item, like PrintPreview/Comparison/Versions.

observability._note: Consumed by OpenRegister's AppHost observability engine (ADR-006 / ADR-040). The GenericHealthController + GenericMetricsController read this block to serve /api/health (public) and /api/metrics (admin-only). Replaces the bespoke HealthController/MetricsController/MetricsCollector deleted in build/adopt-apphost-2026-06-16.

steps.title: Welcome to Filinq
steps.body: Let's take a quick spin through your document workspace. We'll set up a template and a signing request together so you can see how the pieces fit, and you'll add each record yourself.
Templates are the reusable documents you generate, anonymise and send. Open Templates from the menu to get started.
Add your first template. Give it a name and save. You can edit its content and reuse it for documents and signing requests later.
steps.task: Click New and save a template

steps.body: Signing requests track documents sent out for signature. Open Signing Requests from the menu.
steps.task: Click Signing Requests in the menu

steps.body: Create your first signing request. Name it and save. From here you can attach a document and track its signatures.
steps.task: Click New and save a signing request

steps.title: Where the automation lives
steps.body: Flows are what happens without anyone clicking: a reminder before a deadline passes, a confirmation sent on submission. This is where you read and edit them. Nothing to build now.

steps.title: Your first template is ready
steps.body: You have a template and a signing request. The Dashboard tracks them as your document workspace grows, and the documentation covers the rest.
steps.task: Open the documentation to keep going
